decisions.reason: The original universal output requirement and supremum over all U conflict with permitted failed calls, which supply no trajectory. The repair keeps the declared C1 endpoint map on all U, requires its exact derivative on success, and imposes the same time-uniform delta_IVP bound at every successful call only. This resolves the undefined failed-trial terms without inferring differentiability from a possibly nonopen success set.

The converse in original Proof 3.1 replaces the given starts by samples of an arbitrary BVP solution and then applies uniqueness assumed only at the original starts. The repair keeps the original admissible tuple fixed and states the exact correspondence with BVP solutions having y(t_i)=s_i at every node, including the terminal node. Restriction uniqueness now applies precisely to those given starts. Forward gluing uses continuity and matching one-sided derivatives; the boundary row supplies the endpoint equation. No global uniqueness for other initial states is assumed.

The Newton call explicitly inherits the supplier's root status and Euclidean stopping test with epsilon=tau. For residual blocks r_i, max_i ||r_i||_2 <= (sum_i ||r_i||_2^2)^(1/2), so that status implies the advertised block-maximum bound <=tau. The Definition says only that a root status means this bound; it does not assert the converse or promise a root status for every block-maximum-small vector. The stricter inherited test is compatible. The map has d(N+1) positive-dimensional variables, its midpoint and boundary compositions are C1 on the open nodal domain, and finite-budget/domain/singularity branches are specified by the named procedure.
